overview: White plays a quiet 2.a3 to prepare b4 or c3 and d4 without allowing ...Bb4 ideas, a slow anti-Sicilian. Black can reply ...g6, ...Nc6 or ...d5 and often meets c3 and d4 with ...d5 or ...cxd4. White is slightly passive, as a3 is not a developing move.

white_ideas.idea: Play c3, d4 and b4 to build a big centre, a Smith-Morra or Alapin type of set-up.
Develop with Nf3, Be2 and castle, keeping the Open Sicilian options.

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...Nc6, ...g6 and ...Bg7 and use the extra tempo for ...d5.
Strike in the centre with ...d5 to equalise.

typical_structures.structure: Asymmetric Sicilian pawns (c5 against e4) with White pawns on a3 and c3.

character.notes: Quiet and slow; White avoids theory and Black has easy development.

gambit.notes: No gambit in the main replies; the 'Mengarini Gambit' name is for a rare b4 pawn offer.

soundness.notes: Playable; White spends a tempo and is not worse.

structure.notes: Sicilian asymmetric centre; Black c-file and e4 target.

approach.notes: A rare anti-Sicilian, seldom chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Few theory demands, with simple plans.

sublines_that_differ.name: b4 gambit ideas
sublines_that_differ.how: White gives a pawn for queenside space and the long diagonal.

character.reason: Quiet, with simple development for both sides.

gambit.reason: No material is given in the main replies.

soundness.reason: Playable for White though it spends a tempo.

level.reason: Simple but not a recommended first repertoire.

plans.reason: a3 prepares b4 and queenside space.
